column1: # p95 latency budgets in milliseconds, per scale and workload.
# bench/run.sh --check exits 1 if any measured p95 is over its budget.
# Set on 2026-10-28 at roughly 2-3x Design A's measured p95 (Postgres 16,
# Apple Silicon laptop, 4 clients). Tight enough to catch a real regression
# (the per-row cast bug in PLAN.md section 4 was 5x), loose enough for
# Added on 2026-10-29 (rows after the session-1 block below): the parents,
# nesting and medium-scale budgets, from the serial phase-2 runs in
# workload). Same rule as session 1, applied per workload: 3x the p95 of the
# reference, rounded up to a whole ms, at least 1 ms. The reference is the
# fastest of the three engines on that workload (session 1 had only A), so a
# budget says "an engine has shown this is achievable on this data". Engines
# that miss a budget are listed in bench/baselines/COMPARISON.md; budgets were
# not loosened to fit them. The session-1 rows are unchanged.
# for every engine, not an exemption. The query is a bitmap heap scan over
# about 10,900 all-visible heap pages of documents; Postgres 16.4 skipped the
# heap fetch for them and the current patch releases (16.15, 17.11, 18.6) read
# every page (bench/baselines/VERSIONS.md, Calibration). That floor is the same
# for A, B, C and D: p50 7.5-9.4 ms and p95 8.2-16.1 ms over the 27 large
# p95 spread depending on what else the host is doing. 9 ms was 3x the fastest
# p95 of session 2 on the 16.4 laptop (2.9 ms) and no engine has met it on
# Docker. 20 is above every p95 measured (worst 16.10, A, tag p6) and 2.1x the
# worst p50, so it still fails if the plan regresses (a floor that doubles).
# The old rule (3x the fastest p95, 8.2 ms) would give 25; 20 is stricter.
# Stress shapes (--shape deep|wide) use scale-shape keys, e.g. medium-wide.
# Workloads without a row have no budget.
